- When sentiment is positive (≥0.3) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.  
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by immediate correction, reduce peak by 5–10% to account for over-optimism.  
- If true outcome consistently exceeds forecast by 2–3% over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion bias: next forecast = prior forecast + 0.5×(true - forecast).  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.5), reduce forecast volatility by 10–15% to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.  
- If forecast is consistently 2–3% below true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, increase forecast by 1–2% to correct for underestimation bias.
